newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel H1 recurring net 2.72 bln peso.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel H1 recurring net 2.72 bln peso.

text.p: San Miguel Corp said on Thursday its recurring net income in the first half of 1997 was 2.72 billion pesos, excluding one-time gains from the sale of a brewery site in Jakarta.
Earlier, the food, beer and packaging conglomerate reported net income rose 20 percent to 2.89 billion pesos in the first six months of 1997 versus 2.41 billion a year earlier.

But consolidated net sales fell eight percent to 38.5 billion pesos, and operating income declined 37 percent to 2.73 billion pesos due to the deconsolidation of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI) in April.
San Miguel exchanged its 70 percent stake in Coca-Cola Bottlers earlier this month for a 25 percent stake in Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA).

IF CCBPI had been deconsolidated from San Miguel in 1996, consolidated net sales would have improved 14 percent to 32.8 billion pesos in the first six months, San Miguel said. Also, operating income would have slipped 22 percent to 1.80 billion pesos due to softness in domestic beer sales and intensified spending on marketing beer overseas.

As a result of the CCBPI-Coca-Cola Amatil merger, San Miguel said it had an additional net profit of 560 million pesos, which represented 75 percent of the profits on inventories of packaging products sold to CCBPI.

San Miguel said the contribution of its soft drinks interest to the bottom line was 651 million pesos, which included income from an agreement not to compete with Coca-Cola Amatil in the carbonated soft drinks business in Asia.

Regarding its beer business, San Miguel said domestic sales revenue fell one percent to 12.0 billion pesos in the first six months from 13.1 billion in the face of a five percent drop in volume caused by higher excise taxes.

But international beer revenue rose three percent to 3.38 billion pesos from 3.27 billion. Higher marketing expenses of beer, particularly in China, resulted in a wider operating loss of 480 million pesos in the first half for this segment compared with 191 million a year earlier.
Among its other units, San Miguel Properties Philippines Inc delivered a net profit of 742 million pesos in the first half compared with 142 million in the same period last year.
